article_blocks.text: Strain Type: Sativa-dominant hybrid
Genetics: Haze × Kiwi Skunk
Breeder: Kiwi Seeds / T.H. Seeds
THC Content: 19%–24%
CBD Content: <1%
Terpene Profile: Limonene , Pinene , Caryophyllene
Primary Flavors: Citrus, tropical fruit, herbal haze, pine
Flowering Time (Indoor): 9–11 weeks
Outdoor Harvest Time: Late October
Indoor Yield: 14–18 oz per m²
Outdoor Yield: 16–20 oz per plant
Grow Difficulty: Moderate

Mako Haze is a vibrant sativa-dominant hybrid that emerged from the innovative breeding work of Kiwi Seeds in the Netherlands. Created by combining classic Haze genetics with Kiwi Skunk, the cultivar was designed to deliver the energetic cerebral qualities associated with haze varieties while improving yield and structural stability. The resulting plant quickly gained recognition among cannabis enthusiasts for its bright terpene profile and uplifting effects.

Rather than producing the overwhelming intensity sometimes associated with pure haze strains , this hybrid tends to offer a more balanced form of stimulation. Its energetic mental clarity is supported by subtle physical relaxation, creating an experience that feels engaging yet manageable. Combined with its distinctive citrus-forward aroma, the strain continues to stand out as a refined example of modern haze-inspired breeding.
Genetics and Lineage

The genetic background of Mako Haze begins with the legendary Haze family, one of the most influential cannabis lineages in modern cultivation. Original Haze genetics were developed in California during the 1970s from a mixture of Colombian, Mexican, Thai, and South Indian landrace cannabis plants . These strains became famous for their powerful cerebral effects and complex terpene profiles.

Haze genetics contribute the majority of the hybrid’s stimulating mental character. Plants derived from this lineage typically grow tall with elongated branches and produce airy, resin-coated buds. The citrus and herbal aromas commonly associated with haze strains are also clearly present in the terpene profile of this cultivar.

The second parent, Kiwi Skunk, brings an entirely different set of characteristics to the hybrid. Skunk genetics have long been valued for their vigorous growth, strong yields, and pungent aroma. Kiwi Skunk was selected specifically for its stability and resin production, traits that help moderate the unpredictable growth patterns often seen in pure haze strains.

By combining these two lineages, Kiwi Seeds produced a hybrid that retains the cerebral stimulation of Haze while benefiting from the vigor and productivity of Skunk genetics. The resulting cultivar expresses strong sativa qualities but remains more manageable for growers than many traditional haze varieties.
Effects and Experience

The experience produced by Mako Haze typically begins with a noticeable surge of mental clarity. Shortly after consumption, many individuals report heightened awareness and an uplifted mood. Colors and sounds may seem more vivid as sensory perception becomes more pronounced.

As the experience continues, the strain’s cerebral stimulation remains dominant. Thoughts often feel more fluid and creative ideas may emerge easily. This stage of the experience tends to encourage conversation, artistic activity, or exploration of new ideas.

Over time, the effects gradually settle into a comfortable balance between mental energy and mild physical relaxation. While the mind remains active, the body often experiences a subtle sense of ease that prevents the stimulation from becoming overwhelming. Because of this balanced progression, many enthusiasts prefer the strain during daytime activities.
Medical Benefits

Patients exploring cannabis for medicinal purposes sometimes seek out sativa-dominant hybrids like Mako Haze for their energizing mental effects. The stimulating qualities of the strain may help counter fatigue and improve motivation, making it appealing for daytime symptom management.

Mood support is another potential benefit. The uplifting cerebral experience can encourage a more positive outlook and help alleviate emotional stress. For individuals dealing with mild depressive symptoms, the strain’s energizing character may provide a helpful mental shift.

Although the cultivar emphasizes mental stimulation, the gentle physical relaxation that develops later in the experience may help ease minor muscular tension. This balance allows users to remain active while still experiencing physical comfort.
Flavor Profile and Aroma

The terpene profile of Mako Haze produces a bright and complex aromatic experience. When the dried flower is handled, a burst of citrus fragrance often dominates the scent. Lemon and sweet orange notes frequently appear alongside subtle herbal undertones.

Terpinolene contributes fresh herbal and slightly floral elements that give the aroma its lively character. Limonene enhances the citrus brightness, while caryophyllene introduces a faint peppery warmth that adds depth to the fragrance. Myrcene provides a mild earthy base that balances the sharper notes.

During consumption, the flavor unfolds gradually across several layers. The inhale often delivers citrus sweetness and tropical fruit hints. As the vapor or smoke settles on the palate, herbal spice and gentle earthiness appear, leaving behind a smooth and refreshing aftertaste.
Growing Information

Cultivating Mako Haze requires attention to its sativa-dominant growth characteristics. The plant often develops a tall structure with long branches extending outward from the main stem. Growers frequently employ training techniques such as topping or screen-of-green methods to manage height and encourage even canopy development .

Indoor flowering cycles typically complete within ten to eleven weeks. During this period, the plant produces elongated buds that gradually become coated with resinous trichomes. Maintaining proper airflow is important because the branching structure can create dense foliage if left unmanaged.

Outdoor cultivation can produce excellent results in warm climates with long growing seasons. When provided with sufficient sunlight and space, the plant may reach significant height and develop numerous flowering sites along its branches. Proper spacing between plants helps ensure healthy airflow and light penetration throughout the canopy.
FAQ
What kind of strain is Mako Haze? Mako Haze is a sativa-dominant hybrid created by crossing Haze with Kiwi Skunk.
How strong is Mako Haze? THC levels typically range between 19% and 24%, providing moderate to strong potency.
What does Mako Haze taste like? The flavor commonly includes citrus notes, herbal spice, subtle tropical fruit sweetness, and mild earthiness.
Is Mako Haze good for daytime use? Yes. Many consumers prefer it during the day because its uplifting cerebral effects promote focus and creativity.
Is Mako Haze difficult to grow? The plant can be moderately challenging due to its tall growth pattern, but growers often achieve good yields with proper training techniques.
Final Thoughts on Mako Haze

Mako Haze represents a thoughtful blend of classic haze genetics and modern hybrid stability. By combining the cerebral intensity of Haze with the vigor and yield potential of Kiwi Skunk, Kiwi Seeds created a cultivar that delivers both energetic effects and reliable cultivation performance.

The strain’s bright citrus aroma and stimulating mental clarity make it particularly appealing to enthusiasts who appreciate traditional sativa experiences. At the same time, the subtle physical relaxation inherited from its hybrid lineage helps maintain balance throughout the experience.

For growers and consumers seeking a haze-inspired cultivar that captures the spirit of classic sativa genetics while remaining relatively manageable, Mako Haze continues to stand as a compelling example of modern cannabis breeding .
